name: Crazy Horse Recreational Park
evidence: The park's own Google My Maps property map (embedded on crazyhorsecanoe.com/map; KML export read 2026-10-14) marks every RV hookup: the South Campground's '30 amp electric and water' and '30/50 electric and water - no tents' runs by the office and 'All along the treeline' of the field, the North Campground's 30-amp sites by the riverside track, its sewer sites ('monthly sites') at the far field edge. Plotted on Esri imagery (z18/z19, leaf-off): the nearest RV markers are ~35-50 m from the Buffalo River's bank, behind a riparian grove that holds the primitive tent sites ('South Tents', 'North Tents' along the bank) - a wooded strip in use, so not on-water whatever the 'riverfront RV sites' copy says. The park's own RV-site panoramas (camp-rv-sites-pano.jpg and -2) show the river through the trunks beyond the gravel pads by the office, so riverview holds. The earlier 'main RV row set back ~150m across field' read the outfitter's bus row. Pin moved ~280 m from the north bridgehead on Hwy 13 (35.45933,-87.77536) to the map's 'Office/Camp Store/Lodge' marker beside the South Campground's pads.

name: Holly Park Marina
evidence: The operator's rates page sells 'RV 30amp (Water-Front)' and 'RV 50amp (Water-Front)' at $55 against '(Water-View)' at $45 - a per-site class of its own. Esri 2019-04-27 (WV03) at z19 and Wayback 2018-12-05 (release 32645, leaf-off): the marina is a small wooded point south of the Hwy 21 bridgehead on Toledo Bend; RVs stand under scattered pines and oaks 15-20 m from the point's east shore with open ground between and no road, building or continuous screen, and an open lawn runs to the water on the south-east. The earlier 'continuous treeline shore' read the canopy, not the gaps under it.

name: Scenic View Motel & RV Park
evidence: The operator: 'bringing your own camper and hooking up right on the shore front!' and 'over 100 yards of shoreline' (scenicviewmarina.com). Esri 2023-08-24 (WV02) at z19: travel trailers in the paved lot beside the marina, the nearest at its north-west corner ~15 m from Lone Star Lake across an open mowed strip with a few trees; Wayback 2020-06-12 (release 12457): four RVs parked side by side along that lakeward edge, 10-15 m from the water. No road or developed strip between - the open-apron rule; the marina lawn and dock to the south are a used strip, but the RV row is north of them. The earlier 'not waterfront' read the marina's cabins and docks, not the RV row.

name: Angel Nest RV Retreat
evidence: Our pin (36.5328,-105.2746) sat on a cluster of houses ~900 m south of the park, which is what the earlier evidence described. The park's own site (schema.org geo 36.5403685,-105.2774199 for 28418 US 64) and its RoverPass listing (36.540846,-105.277433) both put it at the compound north of the cross-road ~1 km south-west of Eagle Nest village: red-roofed cabins and buildings with a large open gravel RV lot east of them (Esri z17/z18). WestLake RV (28378 US-64, Google 36.53635,-105.27529) is the separate lot further south. The nearest open water of Eagle Nest Lake is ~700-800 m east across a residential subdivision and the state park's marina complex, so the operator's 'mountain and lake views' are a distant vista, not lakeview. Pin moved ~900 m north onto the RV lot.

name: Stony Fork Creek RV Park
evidence: The operator's 'Creekside spaces' (stonyforkrv.com home page) didn't hold up. Its own pages give 10 full-hookup sites at 2149 Pisgah Hwy and the email okelleyfarm@gmail.com; Google pins the park on the O'Kelley farm west of NC-151 (35.46019,-82.73712). The 2023-02-18 NC911 ortho (Wayback release 20512, 0.15 m, leaf-off, z19) shows a handful of RVs parked around the farm buildings there, 80 m or more from the nearest channel. The 18-site loop just north (Pisgah View RV Park, 2138 Pisgah Hwy, same phone), which the operator's photos also show, keeps its south row behind the loop's own gravel track and a shrub line along a small side stream. East of the highway, a lane of trailers runs toward the main creek, but nothing ties it to this park. No RV pad fronts a creek across open ground, so it defaults down. The old pin (35.4628,-82.7368) sat among houses north of the loop and is moved to the farm.

name: K-Park
evidence: The operator says 'We provide full hook ups and have waterfront lots & private docks' (k-parkswfl.com), and its own aerial photo (home page, '36-Aerial Photo 003.jpg', read 2026-10-14) shows them. RVs stand on open gravel pads at the north bank of Henderson Creek, about 25 m wide and tidal with Gulf access. The bank is riprap planted with a few palms and has small dock shelters at the water's edge; there is no road, building or continuous screen between pads and water. Esri z19 (0.27 m/px) agrees: a gravel drive of RV pads runs south from Henderson Creek Dr, and the southernmost RVs are about 10-15 m from the water. The earlier call came from a 900 m frame that couldn't resolve the pads under the trees. It's a creek rather than a river, so creekside.
